title: Client lifecycle metrics fingerprint + ops slate
body:
Purpose:
This working slate is intended to produce a compact, repeatable "fingerprint" for each customer ahead of QBRs and renewal conversations. The fingerprint focuses on four orthogonal operational KPIs (latency distribution, service availability, effective unit economics, cache effectiveness) and a simple scoring rubric that maps to recommended renewal interventions.

Key definitions (operationalized):
- Latency: measure token-generation latency per request. Primary metrics: p50, p95, p99 measured on end-to-end API call (client -> Redwood edge -> model -> first-byte and full-response). Use request sampling for large customers (5% min).
  * p50 latency target: <= 160ms
  * p95 latency target: <= 420ms
  * p99 latency target: <= 850ms
- Uptime (availability): percent of successful API responses over time window (exclude planned maintenance windows). Use rolling 30d window for QBR context, 90d for trend. Count >=2000 requests in window for signal validity.
  * SLA baseline: 99.9% monthly; QBR amber at 99.5%, red <99%
- Cost per token (effective): total billed compute cost (or estimated unit cost for Dedicated) divided by total model tokens generated in window. Include cache savings (see below) so the metric reflects net token cost to customer.
  * Calculation: cost_per_token = (inference_compute_cost_usd - cache_saved_usd) / tokens_generated
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): fraction of requests where a cached prefix or KV entry avoided full model decode/forward. Measured at the routing/runtime layer.
  * Target cache hit: >25% for workloads with repetitive prompts; <10% implies opportunity for caching or prompt rework.

KPI table (example snapshot for Customer X) - use in QBR slides:

| KPI | Window | Measured value | Target | Flag |
|-----|--------|----------------|--------|------|
| p50 latency | 30d | 180ms | <=160ms | amber |
| p95 latency | 30d | 490ms | <=420ms | amber |
| p99 latency | 30d | 920ms | <=850ms | red |
| Uptime | 30d | 99.94% | >=99.9% | green |
| Cost / token | 30d | $0.00095 | <=$0.0009 | amber |
| Cache hit rate | 30d | 8.2% | >=25% | red |

Scoring logic (simple numeric):
- For each KPI assign: green=0, amber=1, red=2. Sum to get HealthScore (0–12).
  * 0–2 = Healthy (QBR: celebrate efficiencies)
  * 3–5 = Watch (QBR: present optimization backlog + cost saves)
  * 6+ = At-risk (QBR: recommend remediation plan + CS/SE escalation)

Renewal signal mapping (examples):
- Rising p95 latency (>20% increase quarter-over-quarter) correlated with increased complaint tickets and feature rollback requests — treat as medium alert.
- Cost-per-token consistently above cohort median by >30% => economics conversation recommended (optimize batching/quantization/route to cheaper model variants).
- Low cache hit + high prompt repetition => quick engineering win: add server-side prefix caching or client hints; estimated cost reduction computed in playbook.

Recommended QBR agenda snippets based on fingerprint: 
1) Health snapshot slide (one table above + one-line trend commentary).
2) Root cause hypotheses (latency: autoscaling lag, model size mismatch, long-tail tokens) with linked tickets.
3) Action plan (owner, ETA, impact estimate in $/month).
4) Renewal recommendation and negotiation levers (discount for committed capacity, dedicated pool, SLO uplift).

Sample action items (templated):
- CS -> Prod Eng: open tracing investigation for p99 spikes (JIRA: ENG-1210) - owner Marco - ETA 2w
- Solutions Eng -> Customer: pilot prefix caching on 10% of traffic - owner Sofia - ETA 1wk
- Finance + CS: run 3-month cost-ops model for dedicated commitment - owner Priya - ETA 3w

Quick formulas & notes: 
- tokens_generated = sum(model_input_tokens + model_output_tokens)
- inference_compute_cost_usd = sum(billed_gpu_seconds * gpu_price + infra_network_storage_usd)
- cache_saved_usd = estimated_compute_cost_avoided_by_cache (use runtime estimate per saved request)

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Define canonical sampling method for very high-volume tenants (>=50k rps); current 5% sample may bias latency percentiles.
- Establish threshold for minimum request volume to include cost-per-token in QBR (proposal: 100k tokens/month).
- Confirm whether private deployments report exact compute cost or require modeled estimates; sync with Finance.

References & links:
- Example trace bundle: slack://thread/C12345/trace-2026-02-14
- Related confluence (fingerprint methodology): CONFLUENCE-12345
- Ticket backlog for remediation: JIRA-CS-872, ENG-1210

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Keep the fingerprint one-slide for exec-level QBR; attach detailed worksheets as appendix.
- Consider adding an NPS/usage-saturation axis to the fingerprint for renewals where product adoption is the risk vector.
- Finalize scoring weights with CS leadership before v1 publication.

-- end of draft slate (please add inline comments in doc, tag owners in Slack thread)
